Synopsis:
    European long-haul carriers (notably Finnair, Lufthansa, IAG, Air France-KLM) have benefited from Gulf airspace disruption linked to the Iran conflict, as Europe-Asia passenger and cargo flows rerouted through European hubs. The gains are real but their durability is questioned — Gulf carriers are recovering capacity, and analysts warn fliers may return. The key forward-looking uncertainty is whether this traffic diversion is structural or temporary.
